doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Women on the bandstand and singers who avoid hiring a woman
summary: Most singers don't want another woman onstage, with exceptions like Anne Hampton Calloway; some still won't hire women.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well I’ve seen you play a bunch of times now and I was thinking to myself, like I can’t imagine why a band leader wouldn’t want you in their band.
I’m also wondering, is there — I’m trying to think how to phrase this question — do you have to be careful of sending the spotlight towards you?

You know there is, a lot of times, and a lot of singers, in fact most singers, that don’t want me on the bandstand with them. And it’s nothing about music. They don’t want any attention away from what they’re doing, from themselves. So having another woman onstage some would feel is a distraction to them. God forbid it’s another woman. It’s just the way it is. So there are a few exceptions to that. I think Anne Hampton Calloway is one of the coolest women I’ve worked with, you know. She doesn’t care. She’s just so good at what she does, she’s so confident, she’s great. So there are the exceptions to the rule. Most singers aren’t that way. So I generally do not work with any singers. And I can © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

only put it down to that fact, it’s like why have another woman on stage if I can have X Y Z of guy bass players that won’t take attention away from — not that I’m trying to. If the gig is just me accompanying, I’m just in the background doing my work, you know? But it’s just the way it’s perceived from a woman’s point of view you know. But so the sex situation, I’m really, I’m just happy to play with good people. There’s also a lot of people that just wouldn’t hire a girl musician, for whatever reason, still.

Yeah. Still. Yeah. It happens. And does it happen less? I’m sure it happens less. But does it still happen? Yeah. It doesn’t bother me. I still work. I still travel and maybe I don’t want to work with them. Do you know what I mean? It’s like I don’t really care so much about the politics anymore as long as I’m playing with good people and as long as I have the respect of the musicians that I admire. I mean really who cares in the end. You know what I mean? If you start worrying about the gigs you’re not doing it can get really dark and bitter quickly.
